Flock Safety, a privately-held U.S. company, has raised almost $1 billion in funding since its inception in 2017. It creates and sells solar-powerd automated license plate readers (ALPRS); more than 120,000 cameras are in service, installed on streets in every U.S. state. The cameras collect visual data on every single car that passes by, and AI interprets the image and stores descriptions of each car into their centralized database. Flock users can search by license plate, car make and color, or smaller details like bumper stickers and roof racks. The software also uses AI to determine private movement patterns and can report which vehicles have visited a location of interest.
